dedupe_keys.name: urbanfootprint land use scenario planning framework open source v1 x

description: UrbanFootprint is an open source land use planning, modelling and data organisation framework for building and comparing land use scenarios, released by Calthorpe Associates. It covers web-based scenario development and editing on a suite of open source components, customised for initial use and testing by regional planners and modellers at three California metropolitan planning organisations: the Sacramento Area Council of Governments, the San Diego Association of Governments and the Southern California Association of Governments. It was developed by Calthorpe Associates of Berkeley, California, with those planning organisations; the repository read today is the version 1.3 code line, whose README describes version 1.1.1. The source code is available from GitHub under the GNU GPL version 3, free of charge. Caveats: the README read is short and gives no installation details or data, so it is best treated as an archived code base. It is useful as an open example of scenario planning software whose land use scenarios feed infrastructure demand, capacity planning and adaptation studies across sectors; a related record is the Copernicus Urban Atlas.
